title: Product PRD: Unified Inference — Overview, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes (Mar 2027)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the product overview, high-level requirements (PRD), design specification highlights, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and the release notes for the Unified Inference product family as of March 1, 2027. The intent is to provide a single reference for stakeholders (product, eng, go-to-market, support) covering what we shipped, why, and how we will operate it.

Key product names referenced: redwood-api (hosted), redwood-dedicated (reserved capacity), redwood-private (VPC/on-prem), redwood-console (observability), redwood-optimize (cost/perf toolkit).

Goals & success metrics

- Primary goals
  - Make Unified Inference the default product for teams that need predictable performance and flexible deployment (hosted, dedicated, private).
  - Reduce inference unit cost by 30% for average LLM workloads through batching, caching and optimized model routing.
  - Provide first-class experimentation/rollout primitives (canaries, A/B, automatic fallback) to minimize regressions during model or infra changes.

- Success metrics (90-day targets after GA)
  - Onboard 25 paying customers to Dedicated or Private plans.
  - Reduce per-token cost for top 10 customer workloads by >=25% compared to baseline.
  - Latency SLO: p95 token generation latency <= 150ms for short-context (<=128 tokens) on hosted tier; p99 availability >= 99.9% for production routes.
  - Quality/regression: zero severity-1 customer-facing quality regressions tied to model rollouts in first 90 days.

Scope & requirements (PRD)

Summary: Unified Inference unifies API surface, rollout semantics, and operational tooling across deployment modes. Below are functional and non-functional requirements.

Functional requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Notes |
|-----|--------------------------------------------------------------------|----------|---------------------------------------------|
| FR-001 | Single API surface for text generation, chat, embeddings and reranking | Must | Keep SDK parity across hosted/dedicated/private |
| FR-002 | Model catalog with pinned versions and compatibility metadata | Must | Support auto-fallback to quantized variants |
| FR-003 | Rollout primitives: canary, A/B, automatic fallback, and manual rollback | Must | Integrate with redwood-console for dashboarding |
| FR-004 | Streaming responses and tool/function calling support | Must | Maintain identical semantics across runtimes |
| FR-005 | Prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching | Must | Configurable per-customer route |
| FR-006 | Cost/perf recommendations via redwood-optimize | Should | Provide suggested quantization and batching settings |
| FR-007 | Enterprise features: KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, VPC networking | Must (enterprise) | Required for Private deployments |

Non-functional requirements

- Performance: p95 token latency <= 150ms (short-context); sustained throughput per GPU >= 3000 tokens/s for average LLM architecture (batching enabled).
- Reliability: p99 availability >= 99.9% for dedicated SLAs; error budget and SLOs exposed in redwood-console.
- Cost: average per-token cost reduction >= 30% relative to baseline serving stack for top-k workloads.
- Security: customer data encryption at rest and in-transit; audit logs retention configurable per enterprise contract.

Design specifications (high-level)

1) Serving runtime and kernel selection
- Serving runtime automatically selects optimized kernels based on model architecture (e.g., transformer block patterns), quantization format (4-bit/8-bit), and sequence-length distribution.
- Runtime exposes per-request hints: expected max tokens, priority (low/standard/high), and fallback policy.

2) Smart routing and rollout primitives
- Route policy evaluation order: region affinity -> customer tier -> model cost -> latency budget.
- Rollouts are implemented as a policy object attached to a route with the following attributes: percent_traffic, metric (latency/error/quality), evaluation_window (minutes), and rollback_thresholds.

3) Caching & batching
- Two-level caching: prefix-level (per-route) and KV cache (per-session).
- Batch scheduler uses adaptive batching: target batch size scales with arrival rate and latency budget.

4) Observability and operations
- redwood-console will show per-route token-level cost, per-model latency histograms, error rates, and a quality signal tied to synthetic prompt-sets.

Roadmap & themes (next 6 quarters)

Q2 2027 (current priorities)
- GA: Unified Inference hosted + Dedicated (basic autoscaling & SLAs).
- redwood-console: route-level cost dashboards and rollout visualization.
- redwood-optimize V2: automated quantization suggestions for common models.

Q3 2027
- Private beta (VPC) with KMS/HSM integration and audit logging.
- Enhanced batching: multi-model batch coalescing for similar kernels.
- Deploy model-level regression alerts tied to eval prompt-sets.

Q4 2027
- Full Private on-prem packaging and hardened upgrade/rollback playbooks.
- Fine-grained pricing plans for Dedicated reserved tiers (S, M, L).

Q1 2028
- Multi-region smart routing with cross-region failover and capacity spilling.
- Advanced quality guardrails: model explainability hooks and structured output validators.

Pricing & packaging notes

Pricing principles
- Usage-first for hosted to encourage product-led adoption.
- Committed reserved pricing for Dedicated with tiered discounts based on monthly token commitments.
- Enterprise pricing for Private (platform fee + per-inference unit), add-on fees for extended observability and compliance packages.

Suggested pricing (guidance for GTM) — public facing tiers (indicative)
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): $0.0011 per 1k prompt tokens; $0.0022 per 1k completion tokens; embeddings $0.0006 per embedding unit.
- Hosted (volume discounts): 20% off >= $25k/month; 35% off >= $100k/month.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): base platform fee $4,500/month + per-token effective charge negotiated (starting guidance $0.0009 per 1k tokens with 12-month commit).
- Private: platform license $50k/year + professional services for VPC/on-prem integration.

Packaging notes
- Bundles: Developer (hosted only), Business (hosted + Console + Optimize), Enterprise (Dedicated/Private + Premium SLAs + Compliance add-ons).
- Add-ons: Extended observability (90-day raw retention), Compliance (SOC2+ISO audit evidence pack), Model Hosting (custom model onboarding & quantization).

Release notes — 2027-03-01 (Unified Inference v1.0)

Summary: GA release of Unified Inference hosted API and initial Dedicated offering. Key features included:
- Unified API for text, chat, embeddings, and reranking with SDK parity across runtimes.
- Rollouts: Canary and A/B with automatic rollback based on latency/error metrics.
- redwood-console: per-route cost and latency dashboards + rollout visualization.
- redwood-optimize: initial quantization & batching recommendations; per-route savings estimator.
- Enterprise features: VPC networking (beta), KMS integrations (customer-managed keys), and audit log export (S3).

Operational impact and runbook highlights

- Owner teams
  - Product: Aisha Patel (product lead)
  - Eng: Daniel Kim (serving runtime), Martina Ruiz (platform & console)
  - SRE: Priya Nair (incident response & capacity)
  - Security: Owen Blake (compliance & KMS integrations)

- Runbook excerpt: Canary rollout procedure
  1) Create a canary route with percent_traffic = 5% and evaluation_window = 30m.
  2) Monitor rollout metrics in redwood-console: p95 latency, error-rate, and custom quality signal.
  3) If error-rate increases by > 0.5% absolute or p95 latency regresses by > 25% from baseline, automatically rollback.
  4) After 2 successful evaluation windows, increase to 25% then 100% following same checks.

- Rollback thresholds and alerts
  - Auto-rollback triggers: p95 latency > 1.25x baseline OR error-rate +0.5% absolute OR quality-signal drop > 5% over evaluation_window.
  - Pager for Sev1: SRE oncall + Eng owner + Product lead.

Open questions & risks

- Model compatibility matrix: need to finalize verified quantization profiles for 10 most-used open models.
- Cost assumptions: per-token cost reductions depend on effective cache hit rates; we need a Q2 instrumentation project to validate customer-level savings.
- Regulatory: Private on-prem packaging may require additional legal review for certain health/finance customers.
